title: Dual-Path QBR Slate — Exec + Technical (draft)
content:
Purpose and high-level notes:

This doc is a working QBR deck template that runs two concurrent presentation tracks: an Executive (business/partnership) path and a Technical (adoption/ops) path. The intent is to let Customer Success tailor a single meeting for multi-stakeholder audiences — start on the exec path for the C-suite, then split into breakouts or append a technical block for engineering/product owners.

Key goals for the template (what success looks like):
- Re-establish partnership value (ROI / outcomes) at the right level for each stakeholder group.
- Surface operational risks early and provide a clear remediation/runbook for engineering.
- Align on a renewal ask with 2-week follow-up commitments and owners.
- Create a compact "next-90-days" outcome plan with measurable signals of success.

How to use this draft:
- Use the Executive slides for the first 20 minutes if C-level present.
- Skip-or-skim executive slides when the meeting is entirely technical; jump to technical milestones and the risk remediation plan.
- Replace metrics in the appendix with live exports from Redwood Console and the customer’s billing portal.

Slide-by-slide outline (suggested timing included):

1) Title + Meeting Logistics (1 min)
- Title: QBR — Partnership Review (Dual Track)
- Attendees (auto-populate from invite), meeting goal, and expected outcomes

2) Agenda & Track Split (2 min)
- Quick walk-through: Exec track (20m) → shared recap (5m) → Technical track (25m) + Q&A

EXECUTIVE TRACK (20 minutes)
3) Partnership Snapshot (2 min)
- One-slide summary: start date, product modules live, seats/consumption tier, ARR/commitment band
- Snapshot line: "Renewal window: Q1 2025 | Current renewal confidence: 64% (see tracker)"

4) Business Outcomes & ROI (5 min)
- Top 3 business outcomes achieved (quantified where possible). Example bullets: "Reduced inference cost per 10k queries by 18% via batching recommendations"
- Micro-case study: 1 slide on a customer success story (before → after metrics)

5) Adoption & User Health (4 min)
- Usage growth (30/60/90 day), active project count, top features by usage (embeddings, chat, rerank)
- Executive-friendly signal: NPS trend or top-line CSAT if available

6) Renewal Options & Recommendation (5 min)
- Option A (standard renewal): baseline price, minor discount, 12 month term, recommended for low-risk customers
- Option B (enterprise reserved): committed capacity, SLA uplift, 15% discount on compute, dedicated onboarding credits, recommended for high-adoption accounts
- Ask matrix: Renewal target date, renewal owner, and expected sign-off level

7) Executive Risks & Mitigations (4 min)
- Top 3 risks (e.g., regulatory needs, capacity/latency incidents, cost spikes) + one-line mitigation plan and owner

SHARED RECAP (5 minutes)
8) 90-Day Outcome Plan (shared slide)
- 3 measurable objectives, owner, success metric, checkpoint date
- Example: "Reduce p95 inference latency below 450ms for primary model — Owner: Carlos Mendes — Checkpoint: 2024-12-15"

TECHNICAL TRACK (25 minutes)
9) Technical Health Dashboard (5 min)
- Sequence metrics: p50/p95 latency, sustained throughput, error rates, request distribution by route
- Adoption signals: cache hit ratio, average batch size, KV cache lifetime

10) Recent Incidents & Postmortem Summary (5 min)
- Three-sentence incident summaries, current status, residual risk, long-term fix ETA

11) Actionable Optimization Opportunities (6 min)
- Batching recommendations (parameters and expected cost savings)
- Quantization/Model variant suggestions for non-critical routes
- Caching prefixes and TTL changes with expected token-savings estimate

12) Runbook: Immediate Triage + 30/60 Day Engineering Sprints (6 min)
- Immediate: enable fallback model for high-latency spikes, add circuit-breaker at 5% error rate
- 30-day sprint: test and roll quantized variant in staging, create synthetic load tests for night runs
- 60-day sprint: integrate with customer's KMS for Private deployments / end-to-end security reviews

13) Open Technical Questions & Decisions Needed (3 min)
- Cached-context eviction policy choice: TTL vs LRU tuning
- Acceptance criteria for CANARY promotion to prod

Appendix (to share after the meeting)
- Renewal tracker (compact) — copyable text table: 
  Renewal Option | Annual Commit | Price Delta | Confidence | Next Action | Owner | Target Close
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Standard 12m | $120k | +0% | 62% | Send renewal proposal V1 | Jonah Lee | 2025-01-15
  Dedicated Reserved | $210k | -10% off list | 42% | Schedule procurement sync | Priya Nair | 2025-01-30

- Risk Heatmap (text matrix): likelihood (Low/Med/High) x impact (Low/Med/High) with 3 highlighted items and owners

- Action owner RACI (brief):
  - Customer Success: Aisha Patel (owner)
  - Solutions Eng: Carlos Mendes (consulted)
  - Customer Eng: Priya Nair (responsible for procurement)

- Follow-up cadence & templates: 2-week follow-up email template, 30-day checkpoint template, canary test checklist (short)

Renewal confidence scoring (example approach) — short explainer in the appendix:
- Score components: usage trend (30%), feature coverage (20%), technical risk (25%), commercial signals (15%), executive sponsorship (10%)
- Scoring guide: 80–100% green, 60–79% amber, <60% red. Use this to set playbook escalation.

Post-meeting artifacts to produce (owner list + timeline):
- Finalized renewal proposal (versioned PDF) — Owner: Jonah Lee — Due: +5 business days
- Technical remediation ticket bundle (grouped, labeled CS-QBR-<customer>) — Owner: Carlos Mendes — Due: +3 business days
- Exec summary email + 90-day plan — Owner: Aisha Patel — Due: next business day

Speaker notes (concise, copyable):
- Exec opener: "Thank you — our goal today is to confirm the outcomes we delivered, highlight where we can drive more value, and agree on a practical plan to reduce technical risk before renewal."
- When discussing pricing: "We’ve prepared two pragmatic options — one aligns with your current pace, the other secures reserved capacity and offers predictable economics for scale."
- During technical handoff: "Carlos will walk you through the operational plan; we’ll keep the remediation scope tight and measurable with clear checkpoints."

Meeting artifacts & data sources (where to pull live numbers):
- Redwood Console: token usage, latencies, per-route breakdown (export CSV)
- Billing export: monthly consumption + overage spikes (finance export)
- Support/incident tracker: Jira project CS-INC or customer-specific tracker

Open questions / decisions for internal review before presenting:
- Do we push a 10% early-signing credit on the Dedicated option for this account? (finance approval needed)
- Is the customer eligible for extended SLA on a 6-month pilot conversion?

Next steps for our CS team (internal short checklist):
- [ ] Lock renewal proposal wording with legal (Aisha) — due in 48h
- [ ] Schedule technical prep call with customer engineering (Carlos) — within 3 business days
- [ ] Run a dry-run of the QBR with Solutions Eng (Priya) — 2 days before meeting

Notes to self / rough bullets (scratchpad style, keep for iteration):
- Consider adding a micro-deck "migration path" for customers moving from hosted to dedicated capacity (financial break-even chart).
- Add a one-slide "compliance & controls" summary when the customer asks for Private deployment details (KMS, audit logs, network isolation).
- Insert short testimonial quotes on the ROI slide if available (keeps narrative tight).

End of draft — feedback requested: please comment inline or drop notes in the linked Confluence page (confluence:CP-QBR-2024-templates).
